transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Um, well, I came in because I just keep feeling like... like I've really let my family down by taking on this new mortgage. It just weighs on me all the time. And at work—I wait tables—lately, every small mistake I make just feels like proof that I'm completely useless. I just have this constant feeling that I deserve whatever bad things happen to me.
Did these feelings start after taking on the new mortgage?
Yeah, they did. Um, it's been going on for about a year and eight months now. It pretty much started right after I took on the mortgage for the condo.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about lots of different things, not just the mortgage?

No, not really. Um, I don't think I worry about everything. It's pretty much just focused on the mortgage, and then how I mess up at work. I'm not really anxious about lots of different things... it's just that heavy feeling about the condo and letting everyone down.
When your mortgage situation feels less on your mind, do you still feel down?

Yeah, I do. Even on the days where I'm not actively dwelling on the mortgage as much, that... that heavy, empty feeling is still there. For most of this whole time, almost two years now, I've just felt weighed down by it, and the guilt, more days than not. It doesn't really go away.
During this time, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I still like doing the things I usually do, like watching baseball or hanging out with my brother. I just feel... sad while I'm doing them. But the actual interest in those things hasn't gone away.

Yeah, I do. Most days there's just this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It's like... when I'm at work carrying plates, I'm just going through the motions. I smile at the tables because I'm supposed to, not because I actually feel anything good. It just feels pretty empty.
Have there been times since this started when you were away from the mortgage situation and your low mood lifted noticeably?

Yeah, actually. There was a stretch of, uh, several weeks where my mood wasn't especially depressed. I was getting through work a lot better, just doing my job without feeling so heavy all the time. But... even though my mood lifted, I still heard the whispering at the condo. And I still felt like I was being watched over the mortgage paperwork. So the mood got better for a bit, but that other stuff didn't go away.
Before this started after the mortgage, had you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for weeks at a time?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days here and there, like anyone, but nothing that lasted for weeks like this. This is the first time it's been this bad for this long.
Have the whispering and feeling watched ever continued for at least 2 weeks during a time when you were not feeling depressed?

Yeah, that's kind of what I was mentioning a minute ago. There was that stretch of several weeks where my mood wasn't really depressed, and I was getting through work a lot better. But even during those weeks, I still heard the whispering at the condo. And I still felt like I was being watched over the mortgage paperwork. So yeah, it definitely went on for more than two weeks while my mood was actually okay.
